rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so I push obfuscation strength up while keeping the hot linked-list traversal loops in main protectable but not crippled: SUB and FLA get the highest SecurityGain (cheap arithmetic substitution and strong control-flow flattening are the best strength-per-cost here for a small 4-function program), SPLIT gets a high DiversityGain as a near-free diversifier that layers with FLA, and ICALL is favored since main's direct calls to usage/allocate are easy static targets. BCF, IBR, and IGV are enabled at moderate weights with suppressed RuntimeCost so the selector preferentially avoids applying them to the pointer-chasing hot loops (where their dispatch/branch overhead would hurt a benchmark binary most), instead letting them land on cold regions like usage and _start. CorrectnessRisk stays uniformly low-to-moderate everywhere because round 0 showed no ICE or miscompilation, but the size-sensitive SizeCost on BCF and IGV caps bloat given the tiny 1304-byte text section, where even a few KB of bogus blocks would triple the binary and make flattened regions trivially segregable.
